title: Process-Level Trajectory Evaluation for Environment Configuration in Software Engineering Agents
claim: Configuring a software environment from instructions routinely hits diverse, distinct error types that an agent must diagnose and repair step by step.
layout: Left character scene, right 5-tile mosaic of error cards, speech bubbles
description: The left side shows a cartoon engineer at a desk in front of a dark screen. The screen shows README-style install commands with a red 'install !!' failure and yellow text about fixing the error. A crescent moon suggests late-night frustration. The caption reads 'I want to set up an environment for a repository......'. The right side is headed 'However, I meet some problems......'. It is a mosaic of five pastel cards. Each card is titled with an error type: Dependency Installation, File Path or Missing File, Logical Order, Command Usage or Syntax, and Version Compatibility. Each has a small icon, a user avatar with a speech bubble giving a concrete example, and a GitHub logo with a repository name. The cards are green, pink, yellow, orange and blue. The eye goes first to the character and the red error, then to the colorful cards.
caption: The illustration of common problems in environment configuration. When human engineers configure the environment, they often encounter various errors. They should first identify the step where the error occurred and then fix the problem before proceeding to the next step, until the configuration is complete. Similarly, intelligent agents performing environment configuration should possess good planning, perception, feedback, and action capabilities.
abstract: Large language model-based agents show promise for software engineering, but environment configuration remains a bottleneck due to heavy manual effort and scarce large-scale, high-quality datasets. Existing benchmarks assess only end-to-end build/test success, obscuring where and why agents succeed or fail. We introduce the Environment Configuration Diagnosis Benchmark, Enconda-bench, which provides process-level trajectory assessment of fine-grained agent capabilities during environment setup-planning, perception-driven error diagnosis, feedback-driven repair, and action to execute final environment configuration. Our task instances are automatically constructed by injecting realistic README errors and are validated in Docker for scalable, high-quality evaluation. Enconda-bench combines process-level analysis with end-to-end executability to enable capability assessments beyond aggregate success rates. Evaluations across state-of-the-art LLMs and agent frameworks show that while agents can localize errors, they struggle to translate feedback into effective corrections, limiting end-to-end performance. To our knowledge, Enconda-bench is the first framework to provide process-level internal capability assessment for environment configuration, offering actionable insights for improving software engineering agents.
